mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates for equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors seek yield in equities.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, aggressive monetary tightening compresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signal deteriorating consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decline > 0.5% and RSAFS decline > 0.5% in last month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where HOUST and RSAFS both decline >0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment (UNRATE > 7.5%) signals economic distress, prompting anticipated Federal Reserve rate cuts that drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE > 7.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 indicates economic contraction, reducing corporate earnings expectations and generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO < 100.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) falling below 950,000 units signal a housing market slowdown, reducing consumer confidence and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when HOUST < 950.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent rises in inflation (CPIAUCSL) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signal aggressive monetary tightening, compressing equity valuations and driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 230 and FEDFUNDS > 0.15.

mechanism_narrative: Late-cycle economic expansions (GDPC1 annualized growth > 2.0%) signal peak activity, prompting profit-taking and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when GDPC1 annualized growth > 2.0%.
